§ 2Content

§ 3TOOTH — ANATOMY

A tooth is a hard, calcified structure found in the jaws (or mouth) of vertebrates, used for biting, cutting, tearing, grinding, and chewing food.

Tooth Anatomy (parts)

  • Crown — the visible part above the gum line.
  • Neck — the area between the crown and the root.
  • Root — the part embedded in the jaw bone.
  • Enamel — the outermost, hardest part of the tooth (made of calcium phosphate; the hardest substance in the human body).
  • Dentin — the layer beneath the enamel, makes up most of the tooth.
  • Pulp cavity — the innermost soft tissue containing nerves and blood vessels.
  • Cement — the bone-like layer covering the root, anchoring it to the jaw.
  • Gums (Gingiva) — the soft tissue surrounding the tooth.
  • Root canal — the channel within the root containing the pulp.

§ 4TOOTH — TYPES AND COUNT

Total Adult Teeth: 32

(16 in upper jaw + 16 in lower jaw, including wisdom teeth)

TypeCountFunction
Incisors4Biting and cutting food
Canine2Tearing food
Premolars4Grinding food
Molars6Chewing and crushing food

(per side; × 4 quadrants = 32)

§ 5DENTAL FORMULA

Adults: 2, 1, 2, 3 = I, C, P, M (per side; × 4 = 32)

Children: 2, 1, 0, 2 = I, C, P, M (per side; × 4 = 20)

In children there are no premolars (milk teeth = 20).

§ 6Key concepts

  • Enamel: hardest part of the body (calcium phosphate)
  • Adults: 32 teeth (16 upper + 16 lower)
  • Children: 20 teeth (no premolars in milk teeth)
  • Types: Incisors (4), Canine (2), Premolars (4), Molars (6)
